examples.en: Children's powder medicine is mixed with water and taken.
If the powder medicine is bitter, I mix it with syrup.

examples.ko: 이 약은 알약 말고 가루약으로 주세요.
examples.en: Please give me this medicine as powder, not as pills.

examples.ko: 가루약을 먹을 때는 사레들리지 않게 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful not to choke when you take powder medicine.

examples.ko: 감기에 걸려서 병원에서 가루약을 받아 왔어요.
examples.en: I caught a cold and got powder medicine at the hospital.

examples.ko: 가루약이 입안에 남아서 물을 한 컵 더 마셨어요.
examples.en: The powder stayed in my mouth, so I drank another cup of water.

explain: 병원이나 약국에서 '가루약으로 주세요'처럼 약의 모양을 고를 때 써요. '알약', '물약', '시럽'과 짝으로 같이 나와요. 아이들 약은 가루약으로 받는 경우가 있어요.
explain_en: You use it at the hospital or pharmacy to choose the form of medicine, as in '가루약으로 주세요'. It comes as a set with '알약' (pill), '물약' (liquid medicine) and '시럽' (syrup). Children's medicine is sometimes given as powder.

en: to nurse; to tend; to attend

examples.en: The mother takes care of her sick child all night.
I took care of my grandmother for three days.

examples.ko: 아픈 친구를 간호하느라 모임에 못 갔어요.
examples.en: I couldn't go to the gathering because I was taking care of my sick friend.
Nursing patients is hard work.
I'm taking care of my father at the hospital.
Because you took care of me, I recovered quickly.

explain: 아픈 사람 곁에서 돌볼 때 쓰고, 병원에서 일하는 직업은 '간호사'예요. 가족이 아픈 사람을 돌볼 때 '병간호'라는 말도 많이 해요. 아이나 노인을 평소에 돌보는 일에는 '돌보다'를 써요.
explain_en: Use it for caring for a sick person at their side; the hospital job is '간호사' (nurse). For family caring for a patient, people also say '병간호'. For everyday care of children or older people, use '돌보다'.

examples.en: I went to the science museum with the kids on the weekend.
The science museum is not far from my house.
I saw a robot exhibit at the science museum.
This science museum has free admission.
Our school is going on a field trip to the science museum.

examples.ko: 이 과학관에는 직접 만져 볼 수 있는 실험이 많아요.
examples.en: This science museum has many experiments you can touch yourself.

explain: '-관'은 보고 배우는 건물 이름 끝에 붙어요. 박물관, 미술관, 도서관도 같아요. '과학관에 가다', '과학관을 구경하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: The ending '-관' attaches to the names of buildings where you look and learn, like '박물관', '미술관' and '도서관'. It is used in phrases like '과학관에 가다' and '과학관을 구경하다'.

examples.en: We did the high jump at the school sports day.
A high jump athlete really flies high.
His body caught the high jump bar.
I find the long jump easier than the high jump.
This year's high jump record is better than last year's.
I watched the high jump final on TV.

explain: 육상 경기 종목 이름이에요. 비슷한 종목으로 '멀리뛰기', 장대를 쓰는 '장대높이뛰기'가 있어요. 운동은 '높이뛰기를 하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is the name of a track and field event. Similar events are '멀리뛰기' (long jump) and '장대높이뛰기' (pole vault). You say '높이뛰기를 하다' for doing it.

examples.en: On the weekend I went to the public bathhouse with my mom.
Every neighborhood has at least one public bathhouse.

examples.ko: 대중목욕탕에서 때를 밀어 본 적 있어요?
examples.en: Have you ever scrubbed your skin at a public bathhouse?

examples.ko: 대중목욕탕에 처음 가면 조금 부끄러울 수 있어요.
examples.en: Going to a public bathhouse for the first time can feel a bit embarrassing.
In winter, a lot of people go to the public bathhouse.
This public bathhouse has a sauna too.

explain: 일상에서는 보통 '목욕탕'이라고 줄여 말해요. 찜질방과는 달리 주로 씻고 탕에 몸을 담그는 곳이에요.
explain_en: In daily life people usually shorten it to '목욕탕'. Unlike a '찜질방', it is mainly a place for washing and soaking in the baths.

examples.en: A few people arrived at the meeting room first.
Please just buy two or three apples.
I called a few times, but there was no answer.
If you rest for a few hours, you'll be fine.
There are a few eggs left in the fridge.
I moved a few months ago.

explain: '두세'와 비슷하게 대략 몇 개를 말할 때 써요. 관형사라서 '두서너 개', '두서너 명'처럼 뒤에 단위 말을 꼭 붙여요. 단독 명사로 쓰는 말은 '두서넛'이에요.
explain_en: Like '두세', it gives a rough small number. It is a determiner, so it must be followed by a counter word, as in '두서너 개' and '두서너 명'. The form that works as a noun on its own is '두서넛'.

examples.en: It has been half a year since I started studying Korean.

examples.ko: 반년 전에 이 도시로 이사 왔어요.
examples.en: I moved to this city half a year ago.
That went on for half a year.
We promised to meet again in six months.
My friend came back to Korea after half a year.

examples.ko: 운동을 시작하고 반년이 지나니까 몸이 달라졌어요.
examples.en: Half a year after I started exercising, my body had changed.

explain: '반년'은 육 개월과 같은 말이에요. 한 단어라서 붙여 쓰고, '반년 만에', '반년 전'처럼 시간 표현과 같이 써요.
explain_en: 반년 equals 육 개월. It is written as one word, and it pairs with time expressions: 반년 만에 (after half a year), 반년 전 (half a year ago).

en: to be put on the market; to be released

examples.en: The new album comes out tomorrow.
That game was released last year.
The new product is due to be released soon.
It sold out as soon as it was released.

examples.ko: 발매된 지 십 년이 넘은 음반이에요.
examples.en: It's a record that has been out for over ten years.
It hasn't been released in Korea yet.

explain: '발매되다'는 음반, 게임, 책, 물건이 처음 팔기 시작할 때 써요. 음악에서는 '출시'보다 '발매'를 더 많이 써요. 영화는 '개봉되다'를 써요.
explain_en: 발매되다 is used when a record, game, book or product goes on sale for the first time. For music, 발매 is used more often than 출시. For movies, use 개봉되다.

examples.en: When I'm tired, I make sure to take a vitamin supplement.
Swallow this vitamin tablet with water.
I bought a vitamin supplement for my child at the pharmacy.

examples.ko: 비타민제 한 알을 물과 함께 먹어요.
examples.en: I take one vitamin pill with water.

examples.ko: 비타민제도 먹고 있는데 왜 이렇게 피곤할까요?
examples.en: I'm even taking vitamins, so why am I so tired?

examples.ko: 비타민제만 먹지 말고 과일도 많이 드세요.
examples.en: Don't just take vitamins; eat plenty of fruit too.

explain: '비타민'은 영양소 자체를 말하고, '비타민제'는 알약이나 젤리처럼 먹는 제품을 말해요. 일상에서는 '비타민을 챙겨 먹다'라고도 해요. 더 넓게 건강을 위해 먹는 것은 '영양제'라고 해요.
explain_en: '비타민' is the nutrient itself, while '비타민제' is the product you take, such as a pill or jelly. In daily talk people also say '비타민을 챙겨 먹다'. The broader word for health supplements is '영양제'.

examples.ko: 수저통에서 숟가락 두 개만 꺼내 주세요.
examples.en: Please take just two spoons out of the utensil holder.
There is a utensil holder on every table in the restaurant.
The utensil holder is empty, so please fill it quickly.
I washed the utensil holder clean and left it to dry.

examples.ko: 이사 가서 새 수저통을 하나 샀어요.
examples.en: After moving, I bought a new utensil holder.
The child spilled the chopsticks from the utensil holder.

explain: '수저'는 숟가락과 젓가락을 함께 부르는 말이라 수저통에는 둘 다 들어가요. 식당에서 수저를 직접 꺼내 쓰게 놓아 둔 통도 이렇게 불러요.
explain_en: '수저' refers to a spoon and chopsticks together, so both go into a 수저통. At restaurants, the container left on the table for self-service utensils is also called this.

examples.en: Yukhoe is raw meat, so it has to be fresh.
At the restaurant I ordered yukhoe and bibimbap.

examples.ko: 육회에 배와 계란 노른자를 올려 먹어요.
examples.en: We eat yukhoe topped with pear and egg yolk.

examples.ko: 저는 육회를 처음 먹어 봤는데 맛있었어요.
examples.en: It was my first time eating yukhoe and it was tasty.
I was worried whether I would like yukhoe, but it was fine.
I like yukhoe and raw fish too.

explain: '육'은 고기, '회'는 익히지 않은 음식을 부르는 글자예요. 보통 소고기를 양념해서 먹어요. 생선을 날것으로 먹는 음식은 '생선회'예요. '회' 앞에 오는 재료만 달라요.
explain_en: '육' means meat and '회' is food eaten uncooked. It is usually seasoned beef. Raw fish is called '생선회', so the ingredient before '회' changes.

examples.en: My uncle emigrated to Canada.
My family is emigrating to Australia next year.

examples.ko: 이민하는 사람은 먼저 비자를 받아야 해요.
examples.en: People who emigrate must get a visa first.
I haven't chosen the country to emigrate to yet.

examples.ko: 그는 어릴 때 부모님과 이민해서 영어를 잘해요.
examples.en: He emigrated with his parents as a child, so he speaks English well.

examples.ko: 이민하고 나서 처음 몇 달이 가장 힘들었어요.
examples.en: The first few months after emigrating were the hardest.

explain: 말할 때는 '이민 가다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. '이민하다'는 글이나 설명에서 보이고, '미국으로 이민하다'처럼 '으로/로'와 써요. 일이나 공부 때문에 잠깐 가는 것은 이민이 아니에요. 들어오는 쪽은 '이민 오다'예요.
explain_en: In speech, '이민 가다' sounds much more natural. '이민하다' shows up in writing and explanations, and takes 으로/로, as in '미국으로 이민하다'. Going abroad briefly for work or study is not 이민. Coming in from abroad is '이민 오다'.

examples.en: I found a small place to rent near the university.

examples.ko: 자취방이 좁아서 책상을 놓을 자리가 없어요.
examples.en: My room is small, so there's no space for a desk.
My friends came over to my place.

examples.ko: 자취방 월세가 한 달에 오십만 원이에요.
examples.en: The monthly rent for my room is 500,000 won.
I cooked and ate ramyeon in my room.
A rented room is good when it gets plenty of sunlight.

explain: '자취하다'는 밥과 빨래를 직접 하며 혼자 사는 거예요. 밥을 챙겨 주는 '하숙'과 달라요. 건물 형태로는 '원룸'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: '자취하다' means living alone and doing your own cooking and laundry. It differs from '하숙', where meals are provided. By building type it can also be called a '원룸'.

examples.en: This temple was built a thousand years ago.
It is a city with a thousand years of history.
They say that tree has lived for a thousand years.

examples.ko: 천년이 지나도 이 노래는 기억될 거예요.
examples.en: Even after a thousand years, this song will be remembered.
It's special because it's a tradition that has lasted a thousand years.

examples.ko: 천년 전 사람들도 별을 보며 길을 찾았어요.
examples.en: People a thousand years ago also found their way by looking at the stars.

explain: 맞춤법으로는 '천 년'처럼 띄어 쓰는 경우가 많고, '수천 년'은 '몇천 년'의 뜻으로 써요. 정확히 1000년이라기보다 '아주 오랜 시간'을 말할 때도 많아요. 비슷한 말로 '오랜 세월'이 있어요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 정말 오랫동안이라는 뜻으로 과장해서 말할 때 써요. 보통 '살다' 같은 말과 함께 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: An exaggeration meaning for a very, very long time. It usually appears with verbs like '살다' (to live).

explain_en: In standard spelling it is often written with a space, '천 년', and '수천 년' means several thousand years. It is often used for 'a very long time' rather than exactly 1,000 years. A similar expression is '오랜 세월' (long years).

examples.en: My older sister gave birth to a healthy baby at the hospital.
My sister-in-law is giving birth next month.
She's resting at home after giving birth.
Her husband was beside her on the day she gave birth.
To give birth, you need to choose a hospital in advance.

examples.ko: 출산할 때 필요한 물건을 미리 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought the things I need for the birth in advance.

explain: '출산하다'는 격식 있는 말이라 뉴스나 병원 안내에서 많이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '아기를 낳다'가 더 자연스러워요. 명사로 '출산 휴가', '출산율', '출산 준비'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: '출산하다' is formal and appears in the news and hospital notices. In everyday talk, '아기를 낳다' is more natural. The noun is common in '출산 휴가' (maternity leave), '출산율' (birth rate) and '출산 준비' (birth preparation).

examples.en: My younger sibling is a fencer.
I watched a fencing match at the Olympics.
In fencing, quick footwork is important.
I am learning fencing at school.
The Korean fencing team won a gold medal.

examples.ko: 펜싱 마스크를 쓰면 얼굴이 안 보여요.
examples.en: When you wear a fencing mask, your face is not visible.

explain: 펜싱은 칼로 점수를 겨루는 운동이에요. 에페, 플뢰레, 사브르 세 종목이 있어요. '펜싱을 하다'처럼 말하고, 탁구나 테니스는 '치다'를 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: Fencing is a sport where two people score points with swords. There are three events: epee, foil and sabre. You say '펜싱을 하다', while table tennis and tennis sometimes take '치다'.

examples.en: My grandfather played the harmonica for me.
This harmonica is small, so it fits in a pocket.
I tried playing an easy children's song on the harmonica.
I heard a harmonica sound and looked out the window.
I do not know where the harmonica went.
I want to learn both the harmonica and the guitar.

explain: 입으로 불어서 소리를 내므로 '하모니카를 불다'라고 해요. 악기마다 동사가 달라서 피아노와 기타는 '치다', 바이올린은 '켜다'라고 해요. '연주하다'는 모든 악기에 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: You make the sound by blowing, so you say '하모니카를 불다'. The verb changes by instrument: '치다' for piano and guitar, '켜다' for violin. '연주하다' works for any instrument.

examples.en: We have lived in the same neighborhood since we were little.
He is a friend from my neighborhood, so we meet often.
We live in the same neighborhood, but I don't even know their name.
We aren't in the same neighborhood, but we live close.
We lived in the same neighborhood, so we went to school together.
The neighborhood people gathered and held a feast.

explain: '같은 동네'와 거의 같은 뜻인데, '한동네'는 가깝고 정이 있는 느낌이 있어요. 보통 '한동네 친구', '한동네에 살다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It means almost the same as '같은 동네', but '한동네' carries a feeling of closeness and warmth. It is usually used in phrases like '한동네 친구' or '한동네에 살다'.

en: to be active; to engage in activities

examples.en: I'm very active in a school club.
That singer is working in Japan.
I was active in a volunteer group for three years.
The weather these days is good for being outdoors and active.
There are many actors working in both films and dramas.

examples.ko: 아이들이 활동할 수 있는 공간이 필요해요.
examples.en: The kids need a space where they can be active.

explain: '일하다'는 직장에서 하는 일 전체를 두루 가리키고, '활동하다'는 동아리, 봉사, 연예계처럼 어떤 분야나 모임에서 움직일 때 어울려요. 가수나 배우가 어디서 일하는지 말할 때도 '활동하다'를 자주 써요. 명사 '활동'은 '동아리 활동', '봉사 활동'처럼 더 많이 나와요.
explain_en: '일하다' covers working in general, while '활동하다' fits clubs, volunteering, or fields like entertainment. For singers and actors it tells where they work, as in '일본에서 활동해요'. The noun '활동' is even more common, in phrases like '동아리 활동' and '봉사 활동'.
